cards.title: True and False are values
cards.body: `True` and `False` are values, like numbers are. A comparison produces one of them, and you can store it.

hi.title: True aur False values hain
hi.body: `True` aur `False` values hain, jaise numbers hote hain. Comparison inmein se ek deta hai, aur aap use store kar sakte ho.

cards.title: Returning a comparison
cards.body: A function can return the result of a comparison directly. No `if` needed.
cards.code:
def is_big(n):
    return n > 100


print(is_big(500))
print(is_big(7))

hi.title: Comparison return karna
hi.body: Function comparison ka result seedha return kar sakta hai. `if` ki zaroorat nahi.

cards.title: Using it in an if
cards.body: A function that returns True or False reads nicely inside an `if`.

hi.title: if mein use karna
hi.body: Jo function True ya False return karta hai, woh `if` ke andar padhne mein accha lagta hai.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: A 30-year-old is told `too young`. Tap the bug.

bug.fix: Line 2 returns True for children. An adult is 18 or more: `return age >= 18`.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: 30 saal wale ko `too young` bola jaata hai. Bug par tap karo.
hi.fix: Line 2 bachchon ke liye True return karti hai. Adult 18 ya usse bada hota hai: `return age >= 18`.

exercise.prompt: Finish `is_even(n)` so it returns `True` when n is even and `False` otherwise. The code below prints `even` or `odd` based on it.
